checks.invariant: On a tag run no inner file of a published asset (LICENSES/* in particular) can differ from the set both Linux hosts rebuilt and the judges judged without failing a gate that attest and publish need.
checks.result: Gate map (gate-map.txt): build job release.yml:163-172 set_key verify hashes every file of build/artifacts against its SHA256SUMS before release.yml:197-198 version.py assets packs exactly the listed files (version.py:155-201); every consumer re-binds the two outer assets by artifact id, digest-mismatch error, the handed-on SHA256SUMS hash and sha256sum -c. same-bytes (release.yml:448-456) compares only the tarball's inner SHA256SUMS with each rebuild's; its wheel step (458-488) sha256sum --strict -c's the wheel's artifacts copy (all 75 listed files incl. LICENSES/*) against that inner list and cmp's the whole wheel with both rebuilt wheels. The runner's _found_and_checked (_artifacts.py:181-218) binds only MANIFEST, the run binary and the zip. But every judge leg extracts the tarball and points WASI_PYTHON_ARTIFACTS at it (release.yml:704-709), and the goal check test_sha256sums_match_the_files (tests/checks/test_v1_1_artifact_set.py:31-33, tests/harness/artifacts.py:38-54) hashes every extracted member, no unlisted or missing file, in shard own-guest on macOS, Linux and Windows (tests/release_shards.toml:88-94); gather G4 is red on any failed check and G2 holds every record's set_sums to the build's (gather.py:179-193, 260-272); gather is in attest's and publish's needs (release.yml:2426-2433, 2489-2493). So a LICENSES/* difference in the tarball fails the gather before signing and publishing; one in the wheel fails same-bytes. No lower-trust writer exists between the build job's verify and its packing (the steps between run the tagged commit's own code). The invariant holds by source, and the observed v0.1.0 assets match.

hardening: release.yml same-bytes (448-456) unpacks the tarball but never runs sha256sum --strict -c on its members, and save-set's set_key verify of the unpacked tarball runs only on branch runs (553); the post-packing binding of the tarball's LICENSES/* (and of the binary a leg does not run) rests on the judge goal check test_sha256sums_match_the_files and gather G4, not on a workflow step. Adding '( cd set/wasi-python-* && sha256sum --strict -c SHA256SUMS )' plus a listed==present comparison to the same-bytes step would bind every inner member in the workflow itself, independent of the judge's shard plan.

The v0.1.0 attestation's certificate names the pre-rename repository ClayGendron/wasi_python; 'gh attestation verify --repo ClayGendron/wasi-python' (the current name) fails closed, while the documented command with the old name (release notes, docs/how-to/verify-a-download.md:20) passes. Consider documenting that the old name is the one the v0.1.0 signature carries, and updating release/version.py verify_note for future tags if the workflow identity follows the rename.

The build job's wheel step copies build/artifacts into the package (release.yml:176) before the tarball is packed from build/artifacts (198), and the zero-patch pytest step runs in between; neither copy is re-verified against the set's SHA256SUMS in the build job after those steps. The judge check and same-bytes S2 catch a divergence today; re-running release/set_key.py verify build/artifacts immediately before 'Release assets' would make the producer's own handoff tight.
